lessons.title: Hazards in the abattoir
lessons.html:
Why safety matters in an abattoir

An abattoir is one of the most dangerous places to work. Workers use sharp knives and saws, work around heavy carcasses and large live animals, and stand on wet, slippery floors. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says your employer must provide a safe workplace, training and protective equipment, and you must work safely and follow the rules.

Main hazards

HazardExample
Cuts and stabsKnives slipping, working too close to another worker
MachinerySaws, hide pullers, hoists, conveyors
Live animalsKicks and crushing in the races and stunning box
Captive bolt stunnerAccidental firing
Falling objectsCarcasses, hooks or shackles falling from the rail
Slips and fallsFat, blood and water on floors and platforms
Strain injuriesRepetitive cutting, lifting heavy parts
Cold and heatChillers, hot water and steam
ChemicalsCleaning and sanitising chemicals
Diseases from animalsSome infections can pass from animals to people through cuts or splashes
NoiseMachines and saws

Personal protective equipment (PPE)

  • White overalls or coat, apron and hair cover.
  • Rubber safety boots with non-slip soles.
  • Chain-mail (stainless steel mesh) glove and apron for knife work where required.
  • Hearing protection near saws.
  • Gloves and goggles for chemicals.
  • Warm clothing in the chillers.

Wear PPE every time, and report damaged PPE so it can be replaced.

Look after your PPE: wash your apron and mesh glove at the end of each shift, store them in the place provided, and never lend them to other workers. Check boots for holes and worn soles that make you slip. Damaged PPE does not protect you.

lessons.title: Working safely and responding to incidents
lessons.html:
Safe knife work

  • Keep your knife sharp. A blunt knife needs more force and slips more easily.
  • Always cut away from your body and away from other workers.
  • Keep enough space between you and the next worker.
  • Never try to catch a falling knife. Step back and let it fall.
  • Carry knives in a scabbard, never in your hand while walking.
  • Put knives in the steriliser or scabbard when not in use, never on the carcass or the floor.

Machinery and stunning

  • Use machines only if you are trained and authorised.
  • Never remove guards. Switch off and isolate (lock out) machines before cleaning or fixing them.
  • Treat the captive bolt stunner like a firearm: point it down, never at a person, and keep it unloaded when not in use.
  • Stay clear of overhead rails and moving carcasses.

Good habits

  • Clean up spills and fat to prevent slips.
  • Lift with your legs, not your back, and ask for help with heavy loads.
  • Stretch and rotate tasks where the abattoir allows, to reduce strain.
  • Never come to work under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

If there is an incident

  1. Stop work and make the area safe; stop the line if needed.
  2. Call the first aider. For a bleeding cut, press firmly on the wound with a clean pad. First aid must only be given by people trained by an accredited provider.
  3. Tell your supervisor, and report every injury, even a small cut. Cuts can become infected.
  4. The injury must be recorded, and you may be covered under COIDA.

Know where the emergency stops, fire extinguishers, first aid box and exits are in your area.

Key points

  • The OHS Act requires a safe workplace and safe behaviour from workers.
  • Main hazards are knives, machines, live animals, slippery floors and strain.
  • Wear PPE, including mesh gloves and non-slip boots.
  • Cut away from yourself and never catch a falling knife.
  • Lock out machines before cleaning and report every injury.
